headline: New Windsor Locks train station will add weekend Bradley Airport bus service
dek: The $121.2 million downtown station begins CTrail Hartford Line and Amtrak service Sunday, with more frequent weekday buses and a new weekend connection to Bradley International Airport.
body: A new Windsor Locks train station will open for CTrail Hartford Line and Amtrak passengers Sunday, Oct. 18, giving the town a downtown rail stop and adding a more direct public-transit connection to Bradley International Airport. State and local officials held a ribbon-cutting Tuesday at the station at 231 Main Street, according to the [Connecticut Department of Transportation](https://portal.ct.gov/dot/ctdot-press-releases/2026/governor-lamont-announces-grand-opening-of-the-new-windsor-locks-train-station).

The station relocates passenger rail and bus service from the existing South Main Street area to a central site near downtown housing, businesses, Windsor Locks Town Hall and the public library. That move makes the project more than a platform replacement: Connecticut officials are presenting it as part of a broader effort to put transportation at the center of the town’s redevelopment and make it easier for residents, commuters and visitors to reach the region without driving the entire trip.

The most immediate change for air travelers will be on CTtransit Route 24. The bus will connect the new station with Terminal A at Bradley in about 12 minutes, with service every 20 minutes on weekdays and every 40 minutes on weekends. Weekend service is new. The [CTtransit service notice](https://www.cttransit.com/services/service-adjustments) says buses will run approximately from 6 a.m. to 11:30 p.m. on Saturdays and Sundays, while weekday Route 24 service will move to the new station and no longer serve the former station or the Windsor Locks Park & Ride for those connections.

Other bus changes are also tied to the opening. CTtransit Route 96E will serve the station on weekday trips linking the area with East Windsor, South Windsor and East Hartford. Routes 905 and 905W will add a stop at the station while continuing to serve the Windsor Locks Park & Ride, creating a transfer point for Route 24 airport buses. The Enfield Square Park & Ride is scheduled to close Saturday, Oct. 17; CTtransit directs current users to the Windsor Locks Park & Ride and says service to Enfield will be reduced to eight weekday round trips and three weekend round trips.

Rail service will begin with 31 weekday trains, 23 trains on Saturdays and 24 on Sundays, according to CTDOT. Weekend trains are scheduled to begin at 6:19 a.m., while weekday service begins at 4:53 a.m. Those figures describe the planned service pattern at opening, but the Hartford Line warns that construction-related schedule changes are continuing through the fall. Its current notice says trip-planning apps and station displays may show incorrect train times from Oct. 10 through Oct. 30, so passengers should check the line’s own schedule and service alerts before leaving.

The station includes 160 parking spaces, electric-vehicle chargers, bicycle racks, a dedicated bus area and an approximately 500-foot platform designed for accessible level boarding. CTDOT also lists heated waiting areas, canopies, Wi-Fi, seating, ticket machines, passenger-information displays and emergency call boxes among the amenities. Amtrak has separately posted an alert confirming that its Windsor Locks station location changes on Oct. 18; its station page describes the facility as unstaffed, so travelers should plan to arrive with tickets already purchased.

The overall project is valued at $121.2 million. CTDOT says $46.1 million covers station and roadway improvements and $75.1 million covers track and pedestrian-bridge work, with about 85% of the funding coming from the state and 15% from federal sources. The work includes rebuilding about 1,800 feet of Main Street, improving sidewalks and drainage, adding a multiuse trail and building a pedestrian bridge over the Windsor Locks Canal.

The transportation benefits will arrive before the construction is finished. Track work remains underway, and CTDOT expects full project completion in spring 2028. The railroad portion includes reconstruction of about 5,700 feet of Track 1, roughly 4,400 feet of new bypass Track 2, and upgrades to signals, crossings and train-control systems. Those improvements are intended to increase reliability and operating flexibility, but they also explain why riders should expect changing schedules while the corridor work continues.

Commissioner Garrett Eucalitto told WTIC that the state forecasts 43,000 passenger trips a year at the station by 2030. That is a projection, not a measure of current ridership, and the station’s longer-term effect will depend on how well rail, airport buses and downtown development work together. For now, the confirmed change is simpler: beginning Sunday, Windsor Locks rail passengers will use the new downtown station, and Bradley travelers will have a weekend bus option that did not exist at the former stop.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: New Windsor Locks train station adds Bradley Airport bus link
seoDescription: A new Windsor Locks station opens Oct. 18 with CTrail, Amtrak and expanded CTtransit Route 24 service to Bradley International Airport.
